title: Marketing | AI Unlocks Strategic Potential
summary: AI is rapidly reshaping marketing, yet many marketers still struggle to use its power well. Some automate routine tasks and generate content; the real leverage sits in the hardest strategic problems.
author: Unique Research
html:
Unique Research · Marketing · December 26, 2024

AI is rapidly reshaping marketing, yet many marketers still struggle to use its power well. Some automate routine tasks and generate content; the real leverage sits in the hardest strategic problems.

Brian Watroba, CTO at a top marketing firm, argues that AI’s leverage scales with the user’s skill — like a master pianist on a Steinway. Skilled practitioners orchestrate models for complex marketing problems. Different models shine at different jobs — compute and logic, nuanced writing, creative work. Tuning each model’s “temperature” dials creativity vs. conservatism.

Most marketers still see only ChatGPT — one instrument among many. They blame a broken piano for an unskilled player, missing how capabilities keep expanding. As AI grows more sophisticated, advantage goes to marketers who ask smarter questions than rivals.

Example: don’t only measure brand awareness — track mental availability: whether consumers think of the brand in a specific purchase context. Traditional strategy work is costly and slow; AI for segmentation, targeting, and goal-setting lets teams test strategic combinations quickly and adjust as markets shift.

Despite the hype, true potential is underused. Those who master the AI “symphony” will lead marketing’s next chapter; those who dismiss it as overhyped risk falling behind. AI meeting martech is not a fad — it is a structural reset.

Using AI for marketing strategy

AI spans data-driven decisions, personalization, and automation — lifting efficiency and customer experience. The data revolution gives marketers tools to process volume and extract insight. Machine learning, NLP, and mining help — but quality, integration across sources, and privacy remain hard.

Ahead: predictive analytics, conversational AI, and content generation will redefine the landscape. Firms that put AI at the core of martech will meet digital-market demand better. Hesitation persists, yet brands increasingly adopt AI for creative and ops.

A beverage giant’s AI remake of a famous holiday ad won praise for quality; a Cannes spot was made entirely with cutting-edge text-to-video. Leaders use AI for visuals that match human concepts and for vivid creatives (e.g., animals up for adoption). Ops gains are large too — chatbots that do the work of hundreds of humans.

Agency investment has been strong — hundreds of millions committed. A Forrester survey shows ad executives widely engaged with generative AI for precision and message customization. Worries remain: many multinationals are uneasy about how agencies use GenAI. Legal, ethical, and reputational risk; clients still value the human element in storytelling.

As AI evolves, its role in creative and operational advertising grows clearer — a tool for brands to solve real problems at lower cost while keeping human creativity central to brand building.

— END —
